page.layout: Running head across the top, with the page number at the top right. Below it, two circular portrait medallions side by side, each with an inscription around its edge. Below them, one column of running text, with no marginal notes and no text below the main text.

main_text.p: HIERONYMVS Sauonarola Ferrariensis ex ordine diui Dominici cucullatus, usque adeo austera vitæ disciplina, ac erudito subtilisque ingenio, & in sacris concionibus admirabili facundia valuit, ut populum instaurandis religionibus deditum, & tū nouo receptæ libertatis gaudio gestienté, quò vellet facilè impelleret, priuatisque familiariū, ac ipsis quoque summi magistratus consilijs misceretur. Scripsit quadragesimale vnū lib. r.[?] super Psalmos pœnitentiales commentū: super prophetas multos commētatus est. Prophetiā quoque emisit, qua multa de hoc nostro ævo, regnorúmque commotione prędixit. Alia quoque multa scripsit. Futura prędicere, veluti diuino ad flatū numine credebant: sed ambitione non caruit & capitale iudiciū de suspectis nobilissimis septem ciuibus, sęua sententia pręcipitauit: unde, cùm mores Alexandri summi Pontificis acerbè reprehederet, sacrosanctam potestatem in dubiū deuocauit: tandem reus maiestatis, deposcēte Pontifice, comprehensus miserabili supplicio affectus est, anno salutis humanæ 1499.

THOMAS Morus, natione Anglus vir doctus & clarus, Cantuariensis Archiepiscopus, exilio primū à rege Angliæ damnatus, post etiam capitali supplicio affectus fuit circa annū salutis, 1535. quod furentis regis Henrici octaui (qui eū paulò ante ad summos honores extulerat, tanquam virtutis eximiæ admirator) nefariæ libidini, adulari noluisset. Iani vitalis de eo extat epitaphium quod sequitur,

p.i: Dum Morus immerita submittit colla securi, Et fluit occasum, pignora chara suum, Immo, ait, infandi vitam deflete tyranni, Non moritur, facinus qui graue, morte fugit.

main_text.p: Hic clarus literarum Græcarum & Latinarum cognitione, Dialogos aliquot Luciani transtulit. Fecit Utopiam, & multa egregia epigrammata scripsit.

page.notes: Woodcut medallion inscriptions transcribed as far as legible; the right one ends in an unclear mark ("ANG.S"). Page number reads as "211" but the final digits are slightly unclear. "lib. r." may be "lib. I." or "lib. 1." in the print. "gestienté" has an accent over the final e, possibly an abbreviation mark. "occasum" in the verse is read as printed. The dates "1499" and "1535" are printed with wide letter spacing. Long s is transcribed as s throughout.
